nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the significance of the marine trophic index in assessing the effect of fishing on fish stocks?
nodes.answer: The marine trophic index serves as a valuable biodiversity indicator for evaluating the impact of fishing activities on fish stocks, providing insights into the health of the marine ecosystem.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some lasting co-benefits of investing in the restoration of marine ecosystems and fish resources, as mentioned in SDG 14?
nodes.answer: Investing in the restoration of marine ecosystems and fish resources can help reduce species extinction, create economic opportunities through employment, and improve food security in the long term, providing sustainable benefits for both the environment and communities.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the purpose of value chain analysis in the context of fisheries?
nodes.answer: The purpose is to understand how the wealth and employment generated by fisheries activities are distributed among different stakeholders from the beginning to the completion of the activity.

On the other hand, the enlargement of harbour-based fisheries economic analysis to a broader economic impact analysis has been done mainly through regional input out- put models (Garza-Gil et al. 2017; Garc a-de-la-Fuente et al. 2020; Raffray et al. 2022), computable general equilibrium models (Akbari et al. 2023), and value chain analyses (de la Puente and Christensen 2024). This latter type of analy - sis is used to understand how the wealth (and sometimes employment) generated by an economic activity is distrib- uted among the different stakeholders involved, from the beginning of the activity to its completion. In the case of fisheries, the aim is to better understand the impact, in mon- etary and employment terms, at each stage through which seafood moves from the boat to the plate, including catching, distribution, processing, and commercialization.
